title: LumenDocs POC Kickoff — Validation Plan, Success Anchors, and Constraints
content:
Background:
LumenDocs is a document automation startup (legal & insurance vertical) looking to augment downstream document extraction, summarization, and question-answering in their claims processing flow. They have a small labeled dataset (~6k documents, mixed text + scanned PDFs) and want to validate: (1) quality of extractive QA for policy/claim questions, (2) latency and throughput on customer-like data, and (3) an integration pattern that preserves PHI protections.

Primary objectives for this 3-week POC:
- Prove accuracy of Lumen-specific QA prompts against a 150-sample holdout (95% CI target).
- Demonstrate an end-to-end call pattern (ingest -> OCR/KV store -> Redwood inference -> business logic) with p95 latency <= 350ms for single-turn QA on hosted API (sizing for dedicated discussed but not required in week 1).
- Validate cost envelope: average token spend per query <= $0.003 (approx) under realistic prompt + context sizes.
- Confirm security posture for PHI: KMS integration and transient cache eviction policy works with customer's constraints.

Out of scope (explicit):
- Full production rollout (dedicated capacity configuration and SSO onboarding).
- Custom model training or fine-tuning; we will use open/Redwood-verified model variants only.
- Complete data migration; sampling of representative docs only.

Success anchors (go/no-go signals):
- Quality: F1 >= 0.72 on extractive QA EM-like metric across the 150-sample holdout and no severe hallucination cases in the top-10 manual checks. Also qualitative stake-holder score >= 7/10 from two Lumen SMEs on a 20-example blind eval.
- Latency/throughput: p95 latency <= 350ms, 99th <= 600ms for single-turn queries on hosted environment with a simulated 10 QPS burst.
- Costs: measured token cost <= $0.003/query on average (prompt + response) with caching enabled for repeated prompts.
- Security/compliance: successful test of KMS-wrapped keys for request-level encryption and documentation of retention/eviction policy approved by Lumen security lead.
- Integration: a reproducible demo (recorded session + API spec) that the Lumen devs can run in their sandbox within 48 hours of handoff.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
1) Automated eval script (repo: lumen-integration/evals) runs and produces a report with metrics and per-sample failure log.
2) A short playbook (PDF) describing the ingestion/OCR + Redwood inference pipeline including SDK calls, error handling, and fallback policies.
3) Runbook for SRE: an ops checklist for rolling back to a cheaper model variant and rate-limiting knobs.
4) Data handling proof: sample manifest showing how PII/PHI fields are redacted or tokenized pre-inference and a KMS key-ID used during the run.

Technical assumptions and testbed configuration:
- Model: Redwood-verified 7B instruction-tuned model (quantized). Fallback path: 3B variant for cheaper inference.
- Deployment: Week1 hosted API in us-west-2 region (customer will test latency from us-east-1 as well). If dedicated is required after validation, we will sketch capacity needs.
- OCR: Partnered OCR (Tesseract + heuristic post-processing) for the initial run; we will note limitations for handwriting and heavily degraded scans.
- Data store: Small KV cache for prefix reuse; Redis-based ephemeral store for this POC only. Cache TTL 10 minutes unless otherwise requested.

Evaluation plan (how we'll measure):
- Dataset: 150 holdout QA pairs + 500 in-scope random docs for throughput tests.
- Metrics: Exact match (EM) for short answers, tokenized F1 for extractive spans, mean opinion score (MOS) from SMEs for answer usefulness, and hallucination rate (binary flag per answer).
- Load tests: Synthetic traffic generator (locally-run script) to ramp to 12 QPS sustained for 5 minutes with 30 QPS bursts.
- Cost calc: Measured token counts via SDK telemetry and extrapolated to 10k queries/day.

Workshop & kickoff agenda (90 minutes, suggested):
- 00-05 min: Quick intros & POC goals review (Aisha)
- 05-20 min: Lumen product context and key success metrics (Lumen PM)
- 20-35 min: Proposed integration architecture (Maya)
- 35-50 min: Eval plan and sample prompts (Ben)
- 50-70 min: Security & data handling checklist (Derek + Priya)
- 70-85 min: Operational SLOs, rollback and incident playbook (SRE rep)
- 85-90 min: Immediate next steps & action items (capture owners + due dates)

Roles & responsibilities:
- Aisha Rahman (SE lead): POC owner, primary contact, delivery sign-off.
- Ben Cooper (ML eng): eval harness, prompt engineering, metrics scripts.
- Maya Chen (Solutions Eng): integration wiring, demo app, SDK examples.
- Derek O'Neill (Security): KMS setup, data retention policy.
- Priya Shah (Customer Success): onboarding, demo scheduling, SME coordination.
- Lumen contacts: Rajiv Malhotra (PM), Ana Soto (Security), Carlos Vega (Lead SWE)

Milestones (3-week plan):
- Week 0 (pre-kickoff): data manifest + SLA questionnaire completed by Lumen.
- Week 1: ingestion pipeline + baseline eval on 150-sample holdout (deliverable: baseline report).
- Week 2: prompt tuning and caching enabled; cost/latency load tests (deliverable: perf & cost report).
- Week 3: final blind eval, security sign-off, demo + handoff package (deliverable: POC final report + demo).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: OCR quality degrades QA performance. Mitigation: sample noisy docs early, surface OCR confidence, fall back to human-in-loop for those cases.
- Risk: PHI policy disallows any external caching. Mitigation: demonstrate ephemeral cache with TTL 0 and KMS-only transient key usage.
- Risk: Cost estimates miss peak behavior. Mitigation: run extra burst tests and provide options for cheaper variant with graceful fallbacks.

Open questions for kickoff (TODO):
- Does Lumen require on-prem inference for any part of the flow? (affects timeline)
- Exact SLI targets beyond latency: acceptable error budget for p99?
- Are there regulatory redaction rules to apply (e.g., state-level differences)?

Deliverables at handoff:
- POC final report (PDF) with results, scripts, and next-step recommendations.
- Demo repo: github.com/redwood-inference/lumen-integration with README + runbook.
- Short deck for Lumen execs (5 slides) summarizing results and recommended path to Dedicated or Private deployment.

Immediate next steps (within 72 hours):
1) Lumen to provide sample manifest + SME availability windows. Owner: Rajiv.
2) Redwood to provision test API keys and seed the eval harness. Owner: Aisha.
3) Security sync: quick call to confirm KMS requirements and redaction rules. Owner: Derek.

Notes & internal reminders:
- Keep prompt audit trail in eval runs (we need to reproduce any failure and show the exact prompt/context).
- Save first-run logs in a separate folder for customer review (avoid redaction until security review).
- Push a lightweight demo recording (screen + audio) at the end of week 3 to accelerate buy-in.

Appendix: Example prompt templates (for team use)
- Short-answer QA: "Context: <document-excerpt>
Question: <user-question>
Answer concisely, provide source span if present. If unsure, say "I don't know; refer to source"."
- Summarization for claims: "Summarize the claimant's key facts in 4 bullets; include date, claim type, monetary amount if present. Tag uncertain fields with [uncertain]."

Record of changes:
- 2025-11-03 Aisha: initial draft
- 2025-11-10 Ben: added eval metrics and load test plan
- 2025-11-18 Derek: security and KMS notes updated

End of doc.
